text:
Philadelphia arrives on the road trip's fourth night after snapping a three-game winless run with a 3-1 win at Vancouver, and Edmonton is closing a four-game home stand off its own 3-1 win over the Rangers. The Oilers are without Isaac Howard, though Colton Dach, who has cleared ESPN's injury report, could play his 100th NHL game.

The numbers favor Edmonton. Our model projects 3.14 goals for the Oilers and 2.64 for the Flyers. At five on five, the Flyers have taken 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their games, against 49% for Edmonton. One caution on the Oilers: their +23 goal difference sits well ahead of their chances, with finishing doing the lifting. Edmonton also takes 4.2 penalties a game, though its penalty kill allows just 0.60 expected goals a game, against 0.69 for Philadelphia.

In net, projected starters Dan Vladar (-0.77 goals saved above expected, meaning saves beyond what the shots deserved) and Tristan Jarry (-1.73) are both below par this season. Vladar was +12.74 last year; Jarry was -4.19.

Leon Draisaitl, with goals in four straight, has a 51% chance to score by our numbers, and Connor McDavid, whose point streak ended at 19 games, sits at 43%. For Philadelphia, Matvei Michkov (24%) has been in the headlines, with Daily Faceoff writing that his "ego" is playing a bigger role in the drama than some might think. Trevor Zegras (24%) was part of a Martone-Zegras-Michkov trio PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor called "really dangerous" in a post-penalty-kill test.
